findings.issue_category: hard-coded cloud credentials in user data
findings.description: The user_data script exports a static AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in cleartext. EC2 user data is retrievable by any process or user on the instance via the instance metadata service (and is visible in the Terraform state and the console), so these long-lived IAM credentials are trivially recoverable by anyone who gains any foothold on this internet-facing host.

The ingress rule opens TCP port 22 to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administration to the entire internet. Combined with the public subnet and internet gateway route, this instance is directly brute-forceable and is the primary path to the credentials stored in its user data.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and the bootstrap script installs only plain Apache with no TLS, so all traffic to the host is transmitted in cleartext over the public internet.

The egress rule allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing no outbound segmentation. A compromised host can freely reach command-and-control infrastructure and exfiltrate data, defeating defence in depth.

No metadata_options block is set, so the instance defaults to allowing IMDSv1 token-optional requests. On a publicly exposed web server this permits SSRF-based theft of instance metadata and any attached role credentials.

No root_block_device with encrypted = true is declared, so root volume encryption depends entirely on the AMI default and is likely absent. Data written by the application, including the credentials injected via user data, is stored unencrypted at rest.
The EBS volume is created without encrypted = true and no KMS key, so the data volume attached to the web host is stored unencrypted at rest.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and specifies no encryption, so a durable unencrypted copy of the volume data exists and can be shared or restored without cryptographic protection.

findings.issue_category: missing bucket encryption and public access block
findings.description: The VPC flow log destination bucket declares no server_side_encryption_configuration, no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, no versioning, and no policy enforcing aws:SecureTransport. Flow logs reveal internal network topology and traffic patterns and should be encrypted and explicitly shielded from public ACL/policy grants.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true combined with the default 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway means every instance launched here, including web_host, is directly addressable from the internet with no NAT or load balancer boundary in front of it.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true and association with the route table that routes 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet gateway makes this subnet public by default, so any future workload placed here is exposed without an explicit decision.
